angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 444,552 km at 32.57 pc = 0.18 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 30.7027 +/- 0.0181 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 32.57 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.639 +/- 0.034 solar radii from Filomeno et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5734 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..90F/abstract): 444,552 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.724 +/- 0.009 solar masses from Filomeno et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5734 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..90F/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4750 +/- 100 K from Filomeno et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5734 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..90F/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Filomeno et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5734 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...708A..90F/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5734.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.687, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
